info.name: PingOne Privilege MCPGW — debug
info.description:
End-to-end probes for the Privilege MCP gateway. Run in order. Each request's Tests tab prints the decisive line to the Postman console (View > Show Postman Console).

Two gates sit in front of a successful tool call, and they fail in ways that look alike:

1. ROUTING. MCPGW routes strictly on Host and only recognises the Frontend Name registered on the application object — {{frontEndName}}, which is NOT what the console UI displays. Wrong Host = 'Domain not found' in the proxy log and an empty 200 to the client. nginx rewrites Host for us (map $host $mcpgw_frontend), so requests through {{front}} are already correct; requests straight at {{gwDirect}} are not, and must set Host by hand.

2. AUTH + POLICY. The gateway compares the token's kid against infra-root-jwt. No PingOne-minted token matches until the application carries front-end OAuth config. A console token does match — and then Privilege answers 403 unless a policy grants that user the MCP application. Console policies can be created time-boxed (1h, 2h); an expired one fails exactly like a missing one.

Full account: privilege/PRIVILEGE-MCP.md §2026-08-10 (later): Host routing.

item.name: 1. MCP initialize — NO auth  (expect 401 Bearer Token not found.)

exec: console.log('401 Bearer Token not found. = the gateway wants a token.');
console.log('It does NOT prove routing: on the :8620 agentless API path the bearer check');
console.log('runs BEFORE any host evaluation, so a garbage Host 401s identically.');
console.log('Routing is only exercised once a token is present — see #6.');
pm.test('gateway answers the auth challenge', () => pm.response.code === 401);

item.name: 2. MCP initialize — direct :8620, Host NOT rewritten  (expect the routing miss)

exec: console.log('nginx is NOT transparent — it rewrites Host to the Frontend Name.');
console.log('Bypassing it sends Host: localhost:8620, which matches no application.');
console.log('Expect an empty 200 here, and Domain not found in: docker logs ai-demo-ping-mcpgw');

item.name: 3. MCP initialize — direct :8620, Host SET by hand  (the control for #2)

exec: console.log('Expect the same 401 as #1 and #2 — on :8620 the token check precedes routing,');
console.log('so this pair does NOT isolate a routing miss without a token. Verified 2026-08-10:');
console.log('garbage.nowhere.example.com also returns 401 Bearer Token not found.');
console.log('Postman must be allowed to send Host: Settings > General > turn OFF the restricted-headers guard.');

item.name: 5. MCP initialize — WITH PingOne bearer  (expect kid mismatch)

exec: console.log('The gateway compares token kid against InfraKid=infra-root-jwt.');
console.log('A PingOne kid cannot match until the application carries front-end OAuth');
console.log('config (cyctl --spec-mcp-app-config-resource-o-auth-*). Routing is NOT the issue here.');
pm.test('MCP initialize succeeded (currently expected to FAIL)', () => pm.response.code === 200);

item.name: 6. MCP initialize — WITH console token  (kid matches; expect 403 or 200)

exec: console.log('403 "doesn\'t have access to MCP app {{mcpAppName}}" = auth and routing both passed;');
console.log('Privilege is enforcing POLICY. Grant the user rights on the app in the console.');
console.log('If this worked earlier and now 403s, check the policy has not expired — they can be time-boxed.');
pm.test('reached the authorization layer, not a routing miss', () => [200,403].includes(pm.response.code));
console.log('Non-initialize calls need mcp-protocol-version AND Mcp-Session-Id (from #6).');
console.log('Omitting either produces errors that read like auth failures.');
console.log('MCP spec expects this to be public. 401 here = no bootstrap path.');

item.name: 10. Gateway /authorize (is the OAuth endpoint itself gated?)

exec: console.log('The /authorize strings in the binary are vendored ory/fosite source paths,');

item.name: 11. CONTROL — backend MCP server direct (proves MCP layer is healthy)
12. Console API — read the REAL Frontend Name

exec: console.log('Key is McpAppConfig, not MCPAppConfig — wrong casing reads as undefined.');
console.log('Use FrontEndName.Elems as the Host header / $mcpgw_frontend map value.');
console.log('It will NOT match what the console UI displays.');

item.name: 13. Console API — is a policy still granting access?

exec: console.log('An EMPTY list is why tool calls answer "User … doesn\'t have access to MCP app".');
console.log('Policies can be created time-boxed (1h, 2h) — an expired one fails the same way.');
